title: The Last Sigil
premise: In the valley of Hollowmere, where magic cannot cross the border stones, Wendell Vane survives by stealing memories from travelers and selling them to the memory-brokers. When a mute child named Sef arrives speaking the dead tongue of Vael, a kingdom erased from history, Wendell learns the child carries the Last Sigil — the final fragment of a spell that once unmade an entire nation, and which the moon's thirteenth turn will complete unless the Sigil is returned through the only door out of a country that no longer exists. Hunted by the Pale Choir, sorcerers who feed on erased things, Wendell must choose between the valley's safety and the found family he never meant to build, discovering along the way that his own stolen memories hide the truth of who he was before Hollowmere. In the end, Wendell reclaims his erased identity, opens the door by giving up his most precious stolen memory, and sends Sef home — remaining behind as the valley's guardian, no longer a thief but a keeper.
about_author: Coral Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from people who vanished from official records. She writes about memory, borders, and the families we build from strangers.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He works a traveler's mind at the border stones, lifting a memory of the sea he'll sell for bread money. We see his rules: never steal from children, never leave Hollowmere. The beat is quiet competence masking loneliness — a man who owns everyone's past but his own.

chapters.title: A Knock in Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. On a moonless night, a child appears at his door speaking a language no living person should know. The words burn cold; Wendell's stolen memories shudder in their vials. Emotional beat: fear giving way to an unwilling protectiveness he can't explain.

chapters.title: The Broker's Price
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, with the broker Marench as a menacing presence. He tries to sell a scrap of the child's language and realizes Marench already knows what Sef carries — and has told someone. Beat: the valley's safety is an illusion; Wendell has been marked.

chapters.title: The Pale Choir
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Hooded figures cross the border stones — the first magic Hollowmere has ever allowed — singing a hymn that unmakes what it names. Wendell flees with Sef through the reed marshes. Beat: terror, and the first crack in his belief that the valley protects anyone.

chapters.title: What the Child Remembers
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, rendered in simple, aching prose. The child remembers a kingdom of glass bridges and a mother who sang the Sigil into her bones before the Choir came. Beat: grief as inheritance — Sef is not a vessel but a survivor.

chapters.title: The Thief's Own Theft
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Examining his oldest stolen vial, he finds a memory he doesn't remember stealing: a burning city, a woman's voice calling him by another name. Beat: vertigo — the hunter discovers he may be part of the hunt's origin.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He and Sef slip past the border stones at dusk, and Wendell feels magic touch him for the first time — awful and alive. Beat: exhilaration braided with loss, as the only home he's known closes behind him.

chapters.title: The Inn at the End of Names
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At an inn that appears on no map, they meet Ossa, a one-armed cartographer of erased places, who recognizes the dead tongue. Beat: cautious warmth — the first stranger who chooses to help rather than to sell.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Ossa's POV. She explains the moon's thirteenth turn: when the cycle completes, the Sigil will finish the Choir's unmaking spell, and everything Sef's people were will be gone even from memory. Beat: the clock starts; hope becomes a deadline.

chapters.title: The Market of Stolen Things
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. To buy passage, he steals memories in a lawless city and hates how good it feels. Marench's agents find him. Beat: temptation — the old life fits him like a glove, and that frightens him more than the Choir.

chapters.title: The Choir's Offer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A Choir cantor corners him: give us the child, and we'll return your stolen past, your true name, your erased life. Beat: the cruelest bargain — the price of survival set against the price of a soul.

chapters.title: Sef's Song
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The child, trusting Wendell, sings part of the Sigil aloud and accidentally shows him the burning city — from the other side. Wendell was there when Vael fell. Beat: betrayal and heartbreak; Sef's faith in him shatters.

chapters.title: What I Was Before
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Alone, he opens the old vial and remembers: he was a Vaeli ward-keeper who fled with a stolen fragment of the Sigil, and erased himself to escape the guilt. Beat: self-loathing transmuting into resolve — he cannot undo the past, but he can finish the errand.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Map
chapters.summary: Ossa's POV. She charts the door out of Vael — a gate that exists only in the space where the kingdom used to be, reachable only by walking a road that must be believed in. Beat: quiet courage; the map is drawn in Ossa's own blood-memory.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Reed Gate
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He finds Sef, who has run rather than be handed over, and kneels in the marsh mud to confess everything. Beat: forgiveness not granted but offered — the fragile beginning of found family.

chapters.title: The Choir Descends
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Pale Choir, guided by Marench's betrayal, burns the inn and takes Ossa. The moon shows its twelfth full face. Beat: rage and grief — the cost of the journey made flesh, and no time left to mourn.

chapters.title: The Road That Must Be Believed
chapters.summary: Wendell's and Sef's alternating POV. They walk the impossible road, and it exists only as long as they refuse to doubt. The Choir's hymn tries to unmake their trust in each other. Beat: faith as a literal survival skill; two people holding a road together by holding on to each other.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Vael
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They reach the gate: a door standing in a field of nothing, humming with the whole dead kingdom behind it. The cantor offers Wendell his name one final time. Beat: the climax's threshold — everything he ever wanted on one side, everything he's become on the other.

chapters.title: The Price of the Sigil
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The door opens only for a memory freely given. Wendell surrenders his most precious theft — the memory of the sea he stole in chapter one, the first beautiful thing he ever owned — and the gate swings wide. Beat: sacrifice as transformation; the thief finally gives instead of takes.

chapters.title: The Choir Unmade
chapters.summary: Wendell's, Sef's, and Ossa's POV braided together. Through the door, the Sigil is returned and the Choir's hymn turns on itself, unmaking the unmakers; Ossa, freed, watches the erased kingdom flicker back into the world's memory. Beat: catharsis — the thirteenth turn passes and the moon rises ordinary and whole.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He cannot pass through the door — a man made of stolen things belongs nowhere wholly — so he says goodbye to Sef at the threshold and walks home alone. Beat: bittersweet release; love measured by what you let go.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, one year later. The valley remembers Vael now; travelers bring offerings of memory to his door, and one autumn night a knock comes — Sef, older, speaking two languages, home to visit. Beat: belonging redefined — family is not where you end up, but who keeps coming back.
